What moved: Bitcoin is up 0.5% today (CoinGecko, 13:16 UTC). The NAOS dollar index fell 0.4% on 16 Oct (ECB).

What the markets say: Polymarket shows Bitcoin above $82,000 on Oct 20 is 68% likely; Polymarket shows a hold at the Oct 28 Fed meeting is 87% likely (13:17 UTC). Prices set by traders, not NAOS forecasts.

texto: Bitcoin is up 0.5% since 00:00 UTC and up 1.6% over 30 days.
In the past month its typical daily move was about 0.7%, so today is an ordinary day so far.

What this is: one day's price change on CoinGecko's market feed. What this is not: a forecast. A month of gains or losses says little about the next month, and bitcoin has often swung 10% or more within a few weeks.
On 16 Oct the 10-year Treasury yield was 0.35 percentage points above the 2-year, so the curve is positive, the usual shape. In the last 90 days it stayed between 0.20 and 0.53 points.

What it has meant before: an inverted curve came before most US recessions since the late 1960s, usually by about 6 to 24 months, and it has also given false alarms. In past cycles the curve often turned positive again shortly before a recession began, so a positive curve on its own is no all-clear.

What it means for people: the 2-year (4.74%) follows what markets expect from the Fed over the next two years, and US mortgage and other long loan rates tend to follow the 10-year (5.09%). Together they set the tone for borrowing costs over the coming months.
